problem: Find the area of the finite region bounded between the curve $x=16-{y}^{4}$ and the $y$-axis.
worked_solution:
First, we find the $y$-intercepts of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}16-{y}^{4} & =0 \\ {y}^{4} & =16 \\ y & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we draw a sketch of the region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14032052/assets/488788313bd32999611a520ec26e4ba6fd68a56e0333a7252a0faaf7107cad90.png)

We want to find the area between the curve $x=16-{y}^{4}$ and the $y$-axis from  $y=-2$ to $y=2.$ 
To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}(16-{y}^{4})\,\text{d}y \\  & =16{\int }_{-2}^{2}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{-2}^{2}{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & =16\cdot y{|}_{-2}^{2}-{\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}|}_{-2}^{2} \\  & =16\cdot (2-(-2))-(\frac{{2}^{5}}{5}-\frac{(-2)^{5}}{5}) \\  & =64-\frac{64}{5} \\  & =\frac{256}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
